doc.welcome:
# md-reader

Read and edit **Markdown** with its real formatting: headings, lists, tables, code, quotes, links and images.

## Getting started

- **Open** a file: `Ctrl+O`, or double-click a `.md` (the installer adds md-reader to "Open with").
- **Three modes**, at the top: *Reader*, *Editor* (the Markdown text as it is) and *Split* (both at once: what you type shows at once). `Ctrl+E` switches between reader and editor.
- **In the reader**: click a checkbox ☐ to tick it; `Ctrl+E` goes to the editor right where you clicked.
- **Save**: `Ctrl+S`. If the file changes outside while you are viewing it, it reloads by itself.
- **Theme**: light or dark with the button at the top; in *More ▸ Theme*, also "same as the system".
- **Language**: in *More ▸ Language*.

## Shortcuts

| Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl+O` / `Ctrl+N` | open / new |
| `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+Shift+S` | save / save as |
| `Ctrl+E` | reader ↔ editor |
| `Ctrl+F` | find |
| `Ctrl+=` / `Ctrl+-` / `Ctrl+0` | bigger / smaller / normal size |
| `Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+I` | (editing) **bold** / *italic* |
| `Ctrl+V` | paste: what you copy from Word, Writer or a web page comes in as Markdown |
| `Ctrl+Shift+V` | paste without formatting |
| `F5` | read the file again |

> Updates arrive by themselves; you can also look for them in *More ▸ Check for updates*.

```python
print("hello from md-reader")
```

# Formatting guide Each format, with **how to write it** (the box) and **how it looks** (below). You can type them by hand, or select a piece and use the **right mouse button**, in the editor or in the reader. ## Text ``` **bold** *italic* ***both*** ~~strikethrough~~ `code` ``` **bold** *italic* ***both*** ~~strikethrough~~ `code` Shortcuts in the editor: `Ctrl+B` bold, `Ctrl+I` italic. ## Headings ``` # Big heading ## Medium heading ### Small heading ``` A `#` at the start of the line, followed by a space. Up to six levels (`######`). They appear in the *Contents*. ## Paragraphs and line breaks ``` A paragraph. This line goes below. A blank line starts another paragraph. ``` A paragraph. This line goes below. A blank line starts another paragraph. (In *More ▸ Keep line breaks* you can switch to strict Markdown, where a single break becomes a space.) ## Lists ``` - a point - another point - one inside (two spaces in front) 1. first 2. second ``` - a point - another point - one inside (two spaces in front) 1. first 2. second ## Task checkboxes ``` - [ ] to do - [x] done ``` - [ ] to do - [x] done In the reader, a click on the checkbox ticks or unticks it. ## Links and images ``` [link text](https://example.com) [to another section](#tables) ![description](photo.png) ``` [link text](https://example.com) · [to another section](#tables) Images are looked for next to the `.md` file (for example, `photo.png` in the same folder). ## Quotes ``` > This is a quote. > It can have **formatting**. ``` > This is a quote. > It can have **formatting**. ## Code ```` ``` a code block keeps the spaces ``` ```` ``` a code block keeps the spaces ``` ## Tables ``` | Column | Another | |---|---| | a | b | | c | d | ``` | Column | Another | |---|---| | a | b | | c | d | ## Horizontal line ``` --- ``` --- ## HTML A little HTML also works for what Markdown does not have. You see the result, not the tags, and nothing is run. ``` in red struck through in red underlined, highlighted, H2O, x2
centred
``` in red, struck through in red, underlined, highlighted, H2O, x2
centred
## Copy and paste with Word, Writer… - **Copy**: in the reader, `Ctrl+C` copies with formatting, ready to paste into Word, Writer or an email. - **Paste**: `Ctrl+V` turns what you copied from Word, Writer, Google Docs or a web page into Markdown: headings, bold, italic, lists, tables, links and colours. - `Ctrl+Shift+V` pastes only the text, without converting anything. ## In the reader - **Click** a checkbox: ticks or unticks it. - **Double-click** selects the word (it does not switch to the editor). `Ctrl+E` opens the editor at that spot. - **Right button** on a selected piece: format it without going to the editor. - `Ctrl+Z` also undoes from the reader.
